text:
jun: Quick follow-up to the rate-control RFC thread — we sketched a priority-admission idea but didn't finalize the probation/penalty interface. wanted to capture tradeoffs before the next sprint.

marta: yup. major tradeoff i keep circling back to: hard drop vs soft-deny (503 with Retry-After vs 200 + short response + low-quality model). soft-deny keeps UX for front-end but hides abuse signals. :thinking:

liam: can we design a mode that starts as soft-deny during probation, then escalates to hard-drop if behavior persists? something like a probation window + credit erosion.

jun: exactly. proposal: each tenant has a credit bucket + probation counter. on sudden burst or abnormal pattern, move to probation with small grace credits for X minutes. if requests exhaust grace credits repeatedly, mark as escalated and enforce hard rate limit.

sara: want to call out distributed enforcement complexity. if ingress nodes have local buckets we risk inconsistent probation state across regions. need a single source of truth or strongly consistent token stream.

liam: agreed. but strongly consistent counters mean higher latency on the hot path. maybe use a hybrid: local fast-path buckets + async reconciliation against global policy store. on mismatch, controller can tag tenant with global "escalated" flag that all ingresses poll.

marta: that seems pragmatic. pseudo-config we'd need from policy service:

```
# admission policy
probation_window_secs: 300
grace_credits: 200
escalation_threshold: 3  # number of probation breaches
burst_buffer_ratio: 0.2  # fraction of normal throughput allowed as burst
probation_mode: soft|hard|hybrid
```

jun: important to specify what constitutes a "breach". suggestions: repeated 5xxs, traffic pattern spike > 5x baseline, abnormal token to request ratio, high error-per-token. we should keep it simple at first (spike + exhausted grace credits).

liam: telemetry hooks we need: ingress should emit events: PROBATION_ENTER, PROBATION_BREACH, PROBATION_ESCALATE, PROBATION_EXIT with context tags (tenant_id, region, model, route). these events feed the controller and SLO monitors.

sara: on storage: we can store probation state in the policy DB (Postgres) with TTLs, and cache in Redis for fast reads. writes go to Postgres and stream to Redis via changefeed. avoids leader contended counters in Redis.

marta: abuse mitigation logic: consider adding a "probation scoring" that decays over time. so a tenant can organically recover without manual intervention. score increments on breaches and decays every minute by a configured factor.

jun: ops concerns: how do we surface false positives? we need quick rollback and manual override APIs: admin-mark-safe(tenant), force-exit-probation, set-temporary-exempt. also audit logs for each state change.

liam: for experiments, we should run canary on a slice: keep default on soft probation and pick 5% of traffic for hard probation escalation path. measure user-facing error rates and support tickets.

ops-bot: deploybot: policy-controller v2.1 canary started on cluster=canary-1 (rollout id=pid-20250320-7). :rocket:

sara: ops-bot — nice. next: define the minimal wire API between ingress and policy-controller. my thought: ingress calls policy-controller on first request in a flow with headers {tenant, route, trace} and gets back a decision object with fields: mode, credits, expiry_ts, reason_tags. keep decisions cachable and idempotent.

marta: plus a cheap fast-path local check: if tenant has > burst_buffer_ratio * normal_quota tokens left locally allow immediately. otherwise call controller. reduces p99.

jun: ok action items: 1) marta + sara draft wire API and config schema. 2) liam prototype probation scoring and telemetry events. 3) ops: add admin override endpoints and audit logging. i'll consolidate into a short RFC addendum. target: ship canary next week.

liam: will mock the telemetry shapes tonight. will include sample metrics and sample Kibana queries.

marta: i'll start on the config proto and a tiny SDK for ingresses.

jun: thanks all. tagging follow-ups: @marta @liam @sara :thumbsup:

sara: one more thought — we should add a "probation-preview" dashboard in console that shows active probation tenants with a quick action button. reduces paging during canary.

jun: great — add that to the addendum. done for now.
